subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different kinds of hardware problems appear in these incidents?

judge.implied_focus: Classification of hardware-related incidents by hardware problem type

per_column.name: hardware_problem_type
per_column.rationale: Directly decomposes hardware incidents into a coherent typology (Printer, Monitor, Keyboard, Storage, CPU/GPU, etc.), which is the core of the implied focus and directly answers the query about kinds of hardware problems.

per_column.name: is_hardware_incident
per_column.rationale: A gating flag that scopes the population to hardware incidents; coherent with the focus and explains the NULLs in the type column, though it is a coarse binary restatement rather than an added facet.

judge.rationale: Both columns center tightly on one data-inferable focus: hardware problem classification. focus_coherence is high because there is no grab-bag; both columns serve the same concept. However, structure_quality is only moderate: the two columns are effectively one categorical typology plus its own binary derivative (is_hardware_incident is entailed by hardware_problem_type being non-null), so the analytical structure is thin -- it captures the 'what type' facet but adds no orthogonal facets (e.g., severity/component/root-cause/resolution) to build a richer structure around the focus. The typology itself is at a useful granularity, avoiding both single-restatement and noise, which keeps it above mid. focus_actionability is high because a hardware-problem-type breakdown is directly investigable (e.g., prioritizing printer vs. display issues).
